results.title: New GPU rates from October 5, 2026 | Jarvislabs Updates
highlights:
New GPU rates from October 5, 2026 | Jarvislabs Updates

# New GPU rates from October 5, 2026

From October 5, 2026 at 00:00 IST, new rates apply to NVIDIA H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. They cover on-demand usage and any reserved plan started on or after that date. Current rates apply until then.

| GPU | On-demand rate until October 4 | On-demand rate from October 5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H200 SXM | $3.99/hr | $4.59/hr |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | $2.69/hr | $3.49/hr |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | $1.89/hr | $2.19/hr |

Rates are per GPU-hour, in USD, excluding tax, and apply in all regions. From October 5, the pricing page will list the new on-demand rates, including INR. For new reserved plan rates, contact us at engineering@jarvislabs.ai.

## Why rates are changing

A global shortage of GPU memory (HBM3e and HBM3 on the H200 and H100, GDDR7 on the RTX PRO 6000) has raised the cost of this capacity. The new rates reflect that cost.

## What isn't changing

- Committed nodes stay at their existing price for the full contract period.
- Storage rates are unchanged.

Please contact engineering@jarvislabs.ai if you need help understanding the effect on your account.

results.title: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Up 4.8% in GPU Rental Market — Week of September 7 - September 13, 2026 | AIMC | AIMC
results.author: Lucas Zelko
highlights: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell posted the largest week-over-week median price increase across AIMC's 34 reporting marketplaces for the period ending September 13, 2026, rising 4.8% from $2.09 to $2.19 per GPU-hour. H100 SXM recorded the second-largest move, up 2.8% to $3.38 per GPU-hour, while the remainder of the top ten movers held within a one-percent band in either direction — a pattern consistent with a market in which broad price pressure is limited but individual SKUs are showing discrete movement. Across 7,884 total observations and 114 distinct GPU SKUs, most segments were effectively flat. The analysis that follows examines each major GPU family in turn, drawing on AIMC-tracked pricing and availability data to characterize where movement was concentrated and where conditions remained stable.

results.author: Abhilash John

# fal reprices GPU fleet upward and adds GB200

Fal pricing

H100 $4.50/h list, as low as $1.89/h; H200 $4.50/h ($2.10/h); B200 $6.25/h ($3.49/h); B300 $8.50/h ($4.49/h); RTX PRO 6000 $2.99/h ($1.10/h); no GB200. H100 $4.50/h ($2.49/h); H200 $6.00/h ($2.99/h); B200 $7.99/h ($5.49/h); GB200 $9.99/h ($5.89/h); B300 $12.99/h ($5.99/h); RTX PRO 6000 $4.00/h ($1.99/h).

Every negotiated “as low as” floor rose, by 32% (H100) to 81% (RTX PRO 6000), and every list price rose except the H100’s, which had already gone up in August. The headline H100 rate fal advertises is now $2.49/hr.

What it means for buyers. Negotiated H100 capacity got about a third dearer, and the entry-level RTX PRO 6000 floor nearly doubled. If you negotiated a custom deployment at the old floors, check whether your contract pins the rate before renewal. GB200 is a new option between B200 and B300 at list.
